maria.g: Heads up — canary v3 shows steady KV memory growth when session mirroring + aggressive prefetch are enabled. 5% traffic, 30min run, ~+300MB resident set for the kv cache.
chris.k: I see that in the perf dashboard. pmap/heap shows fragmentation, pprof flame points to slab allocations in kv arena. Not a GC issue.
samir: Wasn't there a threshold tweak last week? I changed CACHE_MIRROR_THRESHOLD 8 -> 16 on the canary config.
maria.g: Yup. Hypothesis: mirroring duplicates prefix entries across sessions because our cache key still includes session id. So reuse across requests is low even when prefixes are identical.
infra-bot: deploybot: rolled out canary v3 at 3087654220 (mirroring + prefetch) — health checks green :white_check_mark:
chris.k: Sample trace (snip):
```
# pprof top
Showing nodes accounting for 224MB, 68.2% of 328MB total
      flat  flat%   sum%        cum   cum%
    72.4MB 22.1% 22.1%     72.4MB 22.1%  kv::SlabAllocator::alloc_page
    44.0MB 13.4% 35.5%     44.0MB 13.4%  kv::prefetch_worker
    32.0MB  9.8% 45.3%     96.4MB 29.4%  runtime::longctx_keeper
```
Looks like page-level waste + duplicated prefix payloads.
elaine: Another factor — last batching heuristic PR increased chunk_size to reduce latency (avg 3% improvement). That reduces requests per second per worker which unintentionally increases long-live KV residency. More time per session -> more prefix entries pinned.
samir: Proposed remedial design: canonicalize cache keys to drop session id when prefix fingerprint matches global prefix fingerprint and when request has no explicit session-sticky flag. Key form: `<tenant>:prefix:<sha1(prefix)>` and keep session-scoped mapping only for session-sticky flows. This should let reuse across requests increase dramatically.
maria.g: Quick mitigation we can deploy now: lower CACHE_MIRROR_THRESHOLD to 4 and enable async slab compaction every 10s. Should bring down immediate memory curve while we redesign keys.
chris.k: Can someone run a replay on canary with `--kv-stats=trace --hotset=20` and attach top-20 hotset after 10m? I want before/after to estimate dedupe ratio if keys are canonicalized.
elaine: I'll run the replay and paste results in #perf. Running with the current canary now.
ops: Filed ENG-1543 (kv-residency-mirroring): includes steps to lower threshold, compaction toggle, and rollback plan. Link: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/ENG-1543
maria.g: Thanks. We should also add a short test to eval harness that replays multi-session identical-prefix traffic to measure reuse. If it shows >2x reuse improvement we can ship canonicalized keys behind a flag. :thinking:
